predecessors.name: Dzungar Khanate
predecessors.text: Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which the Dzungar dossier records as lost to the Qing in 1696

successors.name: Republic of China
successors.text: Jin Shuren 'replaced the khanate' with three provincial districts (Hami, Yihe and Yiwu)

ledger.x: 1696: the ruler of Hami submits to the Qing and becomes the first Jasak Tarkhan.
1696: Kumul becomes a banner of the Qing.
1912: the Qing banner status ends with the dynasty.
1912: the khanate continues as a vassal of the Republic of China.
1930: the vassalage ends with the abolition.
1930: Jin Shuren abolishes the Kumul Khanate.

wars.name: Kumul Rebellion
wars.outcome: Provoked by the abolition of the khanate in 1930 and Jin Shuren's land seizures: rebellion 'broke out on 20 February 1931' and lasted to July 1934; Yulbars Khan appealed to Ma Zhongying.

certainty.note: An oasis banner whose limits the page never describes; drawn soft.
